<pasted_content id="21a6">
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

Use Unsplash for images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.
</pasted_content id="21a6">

finalReport:
The blog is built and running. The front page lists both posts, and each post renders its block grid with no "Could not render" fallbacks. I only checked the HTML and image responses with curl, so I haven't seen the pages in a browser.

**What I built**
- **Modeling, all through MCP:**
  - Five block element types in the Blocks folder: `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock` and `blogPostListBlock`.
  - Two block grid data types: one for the front page and one for posts.
  - Two page types in the Pages folder: `blogFrontPage` and `blogPost`, each with a template.
  - I updated `siteRoot` so it allows `blogFrontPage` as a child.
- **Content, all through MCP:**
  - A media folder "Blog" holding five Unsplash images uploaded from URL.
  - A published front page called "MCP Notes", with a hero block and a post-list block, and the domain `/` assigned.
  - Two published posts: "One Protocol to Connect Them All" and "Building a CMS Site by Conversation". Each has a hero image and a block grid of rich text, image, quote and rich text.
  - I read back the front page, one post and the domain to confirm they saved.
- **Razor:**
  - I wrote it after stopping the site, building against the generated models and restarting.
  - Pages render the block grids with `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`.
  - Each block has an adapter in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml`, which maps to a plain model in `Models/Blocks/` and invokes a ViewComponent.
  - The ViewComponents are in `ViewComponents/`, and their views are in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`.
  - I added a shared `_Layout.cshtml`.
  - I ran `npm install` and `npm run build` in the Frontend project for the Tailwind CSS.

**How to view it**
- Umbraco is still running from `dotnet run --no-build` in the Umbraco project.
- The site is at https://localhost:44317/, and the posts are at `/one-protocol-to-connect-them-all/` and `/building-a-cms-site-by-conversation/`.
- The backoffice is at `/umbraco` (admin@example.com / 1234567890).

**Not working or worth knowing**
- I did not check that `DataTypeSavedHandler` moved the two new block grid data types into `/Custom/...`.
- Both block grid data types are configured with every block at a fixed 12-column span, so there is no side-by-side layout.
- I did not run the Vue frontend or the backoffice extensions.
